key_insight: TIM separates disease-specific image features from temporal changes, then iteratively refines prior and current reports to improve longitudinal radiology report generation.
clinical_relevance: The approach could support more consistent descriptions of disease evolution across serial imaging studies, though clinical benefit remains unestablished.
method: Separate spatial pathology features from temporal evolution patterns.
Generate initial reports for prior and current studies.
Use error-sensitive mutual feedback to iteratively refine both reports.
evidence_signal: On Longitudinal-MIMIC, TIM reportedly outperformed single-image and longitudinal baselines on language and clinical metrics; the abstract provides no numerical results.
watch_item: Refining prior reports could propagate errors across time points, warranting validation and clinician review before clinical use.
paper_title: TIM: Temporal Decoupling with Iterative Mutual-Refinement Model for Longitudinal Radiology Report Generation
